headline: Southborough advanced a $38 million Neary School addition-renovation plan and began navigating steep FY28 budget constraints across town and school departments.
synopsis: The Elementary School Building Committee voted to advance an estimated $38 million addition and renovation option for Neary Elementary School into schematic design after architects found a $15 million base upgrade would leave key educational and mechanical needs unmet. Across municipal and school departments, officials began assembling FY28 budget plans under a projected operating deficit exceeding $2 million, evaluating potential service cuts alongside a possible Proposition 2 1/2 override. The Capital Improvement and Planning Committee began reviewing $2.15 million in capital requests and up to $49 million in long-term bondable projects. Town committees finalized preparations for the October Special Town Meeting, with the Community Preservation Committee advancing the full Peninsula Trail footbridge request and the Advisory Committee recommending $240,000 for water connections near the Parkerville landfill. In development matters, the Planning Board extended its review timeline for the 21 Coslin Drive Costco proposal to December while approving modifications for commercial sites along Turnpike Road.

top_items.title: Neary School $38M addition-renovation moves to schematic design
top_items.why: The Elementary School Building Committee voted 4-0 to advance Option 3 for detailed design and cost modeling. Architects found a smaller $15 million baseline upgrade would leave fundamental mechanical, code, and classroom needs unfunded.
top_items.body: After review by Tappe Architects showed that a $15 million upgrade would yield only $5.8 million in direct repairs once mandated code, ADA, and soft costs were deducted, the Elementary School Building Committee voted unanimously to focus on Option 3. Option 3 is a comprehensive $38 million addition and renovation plan. Tappe will develop schematic designs, exterior renderings, and detailed site costs—including septic, parking, and wetland delineations—ahead of a planned vote at the spring 2027 Annual Town Meeting.

top_items.title: FY28 capital plan reviews $49 million in bondable projects
top_items.why: The Capital Improvement and Planning Committee began vetting preliminary departmental capital requests. Submissions total $2.152 million in direct appropriations and up to $49 million in potential borrowing.
top_items.body: The Capital Improvement and Planning Committee started evaluating preliminary FY28 requests across municipal departments. The plan is dominated by proposed school infrastructure work, alongside major fleet and infrastructure replacements for Public Works, police cruiser and body camera leases, and facilities maintenance. The committee requested detailed quotes, vehicle replacement schedules, and department appearances ahead of presenting its recommendations to the Select Board and Advisory Committee.

top_items.title: Regional school FY28 budget targets $600,000 health insurance savings
top_items.why: The regional school district is developing its FY28 budget under Proposition 2 1/2 constraints, modeling level-service, level-funded, and 3% growth scenarios. Altering employee health insurance plans could generate roughly $600,000 in regional savings.
top_items.body: Subcommittees of the Northborough-Southborough Regional School Committee reviewed preliminary FY28 budget drivers, including rising special education and energy costs. The district is negotiating health insurance plan deductible changes to match state standards, which could yield an estimated $600,000 in savings. Officials also noted that five Algonquin capital projects total $460,000 for FY28, while the retirement of original 2004 high school renovation debt will result in a net $800,000 drop in regional debt service.

top_items.title: CPC advances Peninsula Trail pedestrian footbridge funding
top_items.why: The Community Preservation Committee voted 3-2 to send the $217,318 additional CPA funding request for the Peninsula Trail footbridge to Special Town Meeting without proposed cuts.
top_items.body: Despite opposition from the Select Board and Advisory Committee over total project costs reaching $428,550, the Community Preservation Committee voted 3-2 to support Article 4 as printed. The committee rejected proposals to introduce floor amendments that would have eliminated project contingencies. The Trails Committee prepared voter informational materials emphasizing pedestrian safety along Route 30 and future grant opportunities to offset municipal spending.

top_items.title: Planning Board extends Costco decision deadline to December
top_items.why: The Planning Board voted 5-0 to extend its decision deadline on the 21 Coslin Drive Costco retail and fueling station application to December 18, 2026.
top_items.body: Proceedings on Costco's applications for major site plan approval and special permits were continued while peer review traffic studies remain under preparation. The Planning Board scheduled a dedicated hearing for November 2 to evaluate the traffic engineering reviews and extended the statutory decision deadline to December 18. The proposed project consists of a 167,000-square-foot warehouse and a 30-position fueling station.

top_items.title: School Committee amends teacher contract and notes roof savings
top_items.why: The Southborough School Committee approved contract amendments for Southborough Teachers Association Unit A and reported the Neary roof replacement is nearly complete with approximately $2 million in savings.
top_items.body: The School Committee voted 5-0 to approve collective bargaining amendments with Southborough Teachers Association Unit A, adjusting retirement incentives and aligning the elementary salary schedule with Algonquin Regional High School starting July 1, 2027. District leaders also reported that the Neary Elementary School roof replacement is roughly 90 percent finished and tracking nearly $2 million under its $4.5 million Town Meeting borrowing authorization.

top_items.title: Zoning Board drafts state Zoning Act compliance amendments
top_items.why: The Zoning Board of Appeals reviewed draft amendments aligning Southborough bylaws with updated state Chapter 40A standards for the 2027 Annual Town Meeting.
top_items.body: Town staff prepared draft zoning amendments to ensure Southborough code complies with Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 40A changes that took effect July 1, 2026. The proposed revisions update standards for preexisting nonconforming structures and lots, extend the abandonment period from two to four years, adopt the practical difficulty standard for residential variances, and establish a two-year variance expiration timeline. The draft moves to the Select Board in November for referral to the Planning Board.
